pr_title: fix: Properly load nested Parquet Statistics
pr_body:
This fixes a bug where nested statistics were incorrectly being loaded as if they were proper values.

Fixes #20510.

issue_context.title: `scan_parquet` raises PanicError when using `collect` after `filter`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl


data = {
    "name": ["a", "b"],
    "data": [
        {"title": "Title", "data": [0, 1, 3]},
        {"title": "Title", "data": [0, 1, 3]},
    ],
}

pl.DataFrame(data).write_parquet("data.parquet")

ldf = pl.scan_parquet("data.parquet")

print(ldf.collect())
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌──────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ name ┆ data                │
# │ ---  ┆ ---                 │
# │ str  ┆ struct[2]           │
# ╞══════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ a    ┆ {"Title",[0, 1, 3]} │
# │ b    ┆ {"Title",[0, 1, 3]} │
# └──────┴─────────────────────┘

print(ldf.collect().filter(pl.col("name") == "b"))
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌──────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ name ┆ data                │
# │ ---  ┆ ---                 │
# │ str  ┆ struct[2]           │
# ╞══════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ b    ┆ {"Title",[0, 1, 3]} │
# └──────┴─────────────────────┘

print(ldf.collect().lazy().filter(pl.col("name") == "b").collect())
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌──────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ name ┆ data                │
# │ ---  ┆ ---                 │
# │ str  ┆ struct[2]           │
# ╞══════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ b    ┆ {"Title",[0, 1, 3]} │
# └──────┴─────────────────────┘

with pl.Config(verbose=True):
    print(ldf.filter(pl.col("name") == "b").collect())


```


### Log output

```shell
parquet scan with parallel = Columns
thread 'polars-0' panicked at crates/polars-arrow/src/array/struct_/mod.rs:120:56:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ComputeError(ErrString("The children DataTypes of a StructArray must equal the children data types.\n                         However, the field 1 has data type LargeList(Field { name: \"item\", dtype: UInt64, is_nullable: true, metadata: None }) but the value has data type UInt64"))
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/xomnia/repos/alliander/delta-lake-test/example.py", line 38, in <module>
    print(ldf.filter(pl.col("name") == "b").collect())
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/xomnia/repos/alliander/delta-lake-test/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/frame.py", line 2043, in collect
    return wrap_df(ldf.collect(callback))
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
pyo3_runtime.PanicException: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ComputeError(ErrString("The children DataTypes of a StructArray must equal the children data types.\n                         However, the field 1 has data type LargeList(Field { name: \"item\", dtype: UInt64, is_nullable: true, metadata: None }) but the value has data type UInt64"))
```


### Issue description

If I scan a simple parquet file with a Struct column, I get a `PanicException` when I filter the LazyFrame and collect. I don't get the error if I collect first and then filter, nor do I get the error when I turn the full DataFrame into a LazyFrame first, and then filter and collect again.

(Not sure whether this is a bug or just not supported)

### Expected behavior

To be able to do:

```python
print(ldf.filter(pl.col("name") == "b").collect())
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌──────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ name ┆ data                │
# │ ---  ┆ ---                 │
# │ str  ┆ struct[2]           │
# ╞══════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ b    ┆ {"Title",[0, 1, 3]} │
# └──────┴─────────────────────┘
```

comments:
Yeah - looks to be a bug.

It runs with the predicate_pushdown optimization disabled.

```python
ldf.filter(pl.col("name") == "b").collect(predicate_pushdown=False)
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌──────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ name ┆ data                │
# │ ---  ┆ ---                 │
# │ str  ┆ struct[2]           │
# ╞══════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ b    ┆ {"Title",[0, 1, 3]} │
# └──────┴─────────────────────┘
```
Just ran into this same issue.  Using `polars==1.17.0` until the fix is released, which doesn't crash for me.

This is still happening with the bleeding edge 1.20.0

Passing `predicate_pushdown=False` suppresses the error

> This is still happening with the bleeding edge 1.20.0
> 
> Passing `predicate_pushdown=False` suppresses the error

I installed polars 1.2 from pypi and, at least for local parquet files, I can collect after a filter on a lazyframe from scan_parquet.

I haven't tested it yet on my usual work use case which is parquet files on Azure blob storage, but will post if that still crashes.

@ritchie46 I tested 1.20.0 with `scan_parquet` with Azure blobs and 1.20.0 isn't crashing - but is _much_ slower than 1.17.0 doing aggregations on lazy frames. Things that took 3 seconds in 1.17 are taking 14 seconds in 1.20.0.

We would really need a reproduction example. The original issue does not produce an issue anymore.
